thirdPartyServices.note: Free tier covers up to 5,000 users. You're at 1,000. Safe.

This is your biggest cost. If each resume generation costs $0.05 (2K tokens in, 1K tokens out), and 20% of your 1,000 users generate 1 resume/month, that's 200 generations = $10/month. But heavy users could generate 5-10 resumes/month, pushing this to $50-100/month.
If 200 PDFs/month at $0.01-0.02 each = $2-4/month. But if users generate multiple versions, this scales with OpenAI usage.

growthScaleCosts.breakdown: Hosting scales to $15/month (Railway paid tier). Database might need paid tier ($10/month). OpenAI API becomes $90-300/month depending on usage patterns. PDF generation $30-60/month. This exceeds your $150 budget significantly.

cheaperAlternatives.cheaperOption: SQLite (local file) until you hit 10K users
cheaperAlternatives.tradeoff: SQLite is single-file, no network overhead, perfect for solo app at your scale. You'll need to migrate to PostgreSQL eventually, but not now. Save the money.

cheaperAlternatives.cheaperOption: GPT-3.5-Turbo for first draft, GPT-4 for final polish (optional upgrade)
cheaperAlternatives.tradeoff: GPT-3.5-Turbo costs 1/10th of GPT-4. Quality is slightly lower, but for resume rewrites, it's 80% as good at 10% the cost. Let users opt into GPT-4 as a paid upgrade. Most won't know the difference.
Security Agent warned about this, but if you're careful (sandbox Puppeteer, validate inputs), you can save $10-20/month. Trade security risk for cost savings — your call.

hiddenCosts.explanation: Without rate limiting (which Security Agent mentioned), a malicious user or bug could spam your API. OpenAI doesn't auto-cut you off — you get a bill. Set usage limits in OpenAI dashboard.
Each resume is ~5KB text + metadata. 1,000 users × 3 resumes each = 15MB. Negligible now, but if you store every version, it compounds. Security Agent mentioned deleting old resumes — do it.
Services like LogRocket, Sentry, or Datadog cost money. Use Railway's built-in logs for free initially. Add paid monitoring only when you have revenue.

budgetVerdict.reasoning: Your $150/month budget CAN work at 1,000 users if: (1) You use GPT-3.5-Turbo instead of GPT-4 as default, (2) You use SQLite instead of hosted PostgreSQL, (3) You implement rate limiting to prevent API abuse. But at 3x growth (3,000 users), you'll exceed budget. Plan to charge users $5-10/month by then to cover costs.

reasoning: Your biggest cost is the OpenAI API — it's variable and scales with usage. The Architect's plan is solid but slightly over-engineered for your budget. I've challenged the PostgreSQL and GPT-4 recommendations with cheaper alternatives. The Security Agent's recommendations (rate limiting, auth) actually SAVE you money by preventing abuse. Follow those.
